item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Thursday
item.description: Unemployment down for fourth month in a row, child rights organisation receives hundreds of calls from gang children, Swedes to spend 24.5 billion kronor on Christmas presents and more news from Sweden on Thursday.

item.title: What changes for families in Sweden in 2026?
item.description: From cheaper preschool fees, smaller food bills and changes to Swedish schools, 2026 is set to be a year with big changes affecting families living in Sweden.

item.title: Parenting in Sweden: How to prepare for your child's Lucia celebration
item.description: If your children have just started school or preschool in Sweden or you haven't been in the country for very long, this could be your first ever Lucia celebration. What is it, and how should you prepare?

item.title: Prices of Swedish Christmas foods rise 33 percent in five years
item.description: Typical items used in Swedish Christmas baking like flour, butter and chocolate have seen major price increases over the past five years, while coffee in Sweden has risen by 100 percent since 2020.

item.title: NAKED SHOCK! And the other unique tabloid words you'll see in Sweden
item.description: You won't learn them in your Swedish for Immigrants class and you probably won't even hear them in daily conversation. But you can't avoid them, because they are splashed across every tabloid frontpage in Sweden. Here's what they mean.

item.title: 'I've got nobody here': Stockholm basketball coach deported to Uganda
item.description: Former Stockholm basketball coach Eric Nsubuga, 22, tells The Local of his deportation to Uganda, a country he has not been in since he was 10, where he does not speak the language, and where he has no relatives.

item.title: China defends jailing Swedish-Chinese bookseller after UN release call
item.description: China rejected on Thursday any "interference" in its judicial sovereignty after a United Nations working group called for the immediate release of jailed Chinese-Swedish bookseller Gui Minhai.

item.title: Swedish word of the day: ljus
item.description: Today's Swedish word is one we all need this time of the year.

item.title: 'Contrary to human dignity': Swedish Church slams plan to revoke permanent residence
item.description: The Church of Sweden has formally rejected a government inquiry's proposal that would see more than 100,000 people stripped of their permanent residency permits, condemning the proposal as "unreasonable", "disproportionate", and arguing it fails to protect human dignity.

item.title: Saints, spooks, and eyeballs: An immigrant's view of Lucia in Sweden
item.description: It's mid-December and in Sweden that means Lucia: groups of white-robed people singing with candles on their heads. But what exactly is this strangely beautiful (and beautifully eerie) celebration about, and where did it come from?
